sentences.text: Exploring a research collaboration on Krabbe disease
We are writing to KrabbeConnect, which supports families with Krabbe disease, and would also value the views of Hunter's Hope Foundation.
Krabbe disease is linked to lysosomal enzyme deficiency and the resulting storage of material in lysosomes.
KrabbeCURES and the Krabbe Disease Global Patient Registry include people with Krabbe disease, and the registry is recruiting.
A natural history study of infantile globoid cell leukodystrophy has been completed.
Several stem cell transplant studies included Krabbe disease, two completed and one active but not recruiting, and early transplantation is listed as in development.
A gene transfer trial for children previously treated with transplantation is active but not recruiting.
We would like to explore a jointly designed study on Krabbe disease, shaped with your community from the start: [study question], [design], [sites].
Any participation would follow informed consent and ethics approval, and we would share what we learn with your community.

sections.heading: What we would ask of you

sentences.text: Would you be open to a conversation about whether this idea is useful to the families you serve?
If so, we would value your view on how your community, registry or natural history work could take part, with proper consent and ethics approval.
We are not asking for any personal information about patients or families.
Could we arrange a short call at a time that suits you, perhaps [proposed dates]?
With thanks and warm regards, [researcher name], [institution].
